# BTC-USD (Bitcoin USD, CCC) — Technical Analysis Report
**Analysis date: 2026-11-04** | All exact price/indicator values below are anchored to the verified market snapshot (source of truth).

---

## 1. Executive Summary

BTC-USD closed at **$80,110.81** on 2026-11-04, a **+3.58%** surge from the prior verified close of $77,345.05 (2026-11-03), on the heaviest volume of the past week (~39.95B vs ~22.4B the prior day). The day's range was $75,709.91–$80,746.25 — a 5,036-point span equal to **~2.3× the current ATR (2,160.17)** — a classic high-volume volatility-expansion reversal day: the intraday low **pierced below the lower Bollinger Band (76,033.77)** before the market recovered to close essentially at the middle band (80,188.85, just −0.10% away).

The structural picture is a **transition zone**: price is **+9.47% above the 200 SMA (73,179.53)** — the long-term trend benchmark that was reclaimed during the August rally and protected by a **golden cross between 2026-09-07 and 2026-09-08** (50 SMA: 69,694.32 → 69,958.49 vs 200 SMA: 69,814.41 → 69,866.57) — yet price remains **−2.29% below the 50 SMA (81,986.29)**, which caps the market after October's failed push. Momentum (MACD −1,116.40) is still in a negative regime but the histogram has contracted three consecutive sessions (−479.68 → −422.11 → −179.27), and RSI has snapped from 34.33 (Oct 30) to 49.68. **Bias: neutral-to-cautiously-bullish short term within a larger repair phase; the 50 SMA at ~81,986 is the decision line.**

---

## 2. Market Context — The Past 12 Months (from the retrieved daily series)

The year splits into three distinct regimes:

- **Phase 1 — Distribution & Breakdown (Nov 2025 – Jan 2026):** BTC-USD topped near **$110,639.62** (close, 2025-11-02) and broke down violently: closes fell to $101,590.52 (11-04), $84,648.36 (11-22), ranged through December, rallied to $96,929.33 (2026-01-14), then collapsed late January to $78,621.12 (2026-01-31).
- **Phase 2 — Bear Acceleration (Feb – Jun 2026):** A waterfall decline took price from the mid-$70Ks to the **$60Ks (Feb 5: low $62,353.54)**, a partial recovery in March–April (to $78,268.95 on 04-23), a May fade, and a final June capitulation to the yearly floor — **intraday low $57,747.77 on 2026-07-01** (June 30 close $58,558.86).
- **Phase 3 — Recovery & Repairs (Jul – Nov 2026):** A mid-August impulse lifted price from $64,680.71 (08-18 close) to $78,335.19 (08-21), a September push to the recovery high **$87,363.76 (2026-09-21)**, and an October fade of lower highs (Oct 2 high $87,146.35 → Oct 21 high $84,840.05) and lower lows (Oct 25 low $79,766.83 → Oct 30 low $76,189.88 → **Nov 4 low $75,709.91**).

Critically, the daily structure since early October remains a **downtrend (lower highs, lower lows)** — but 2026-11-04 delivered the strongest counter-trend thrust of that phase, with volume confirmation. This is the first genuine attempt to arrest the October slide.

---

## 3. Selected Indicators and Why (8 total, complementary, non-redundant)

Given a **post-crash repair market with elevated volatility, a downtrend on the daily, and a fresh reversal thrust**, I selected:

| Block | Indicator | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Trend | **close_200_sma** | Strategic regime filter (is the macro trend repaired?) |
| Trend | **close_50_sma** | The immediate dynamic resistance cap; trend-repair reference |
| Trend | **close_10_ema** | Fast trigger line for the short-term reversal |
| Momentum | **macd** | Regime check (above/below zero) after the October slide |
| Momentum | **macdh** | Earliest read on momentum inflection (histogram contraction) |
| Momentum | **rsi** | Exhaustion/recovery gauge (single momentum oscillator, no redundancy) |
| Volatility | **boll_ub** | Breakout/overbought ceiling; paired with verified middle & lower bands for the mean-reversion map |
| Risk | **atr** | Stop placement and position sizing in a 2.3×-ATR-range market |

Deliberately excluded: MACD Signal (redundant with MACD + Histogram; its value −937.13 is available in the verified snapshot and used below for crossover math), VWMA (volume already assessed from raw OHLCV), and additional oscillators.

---

## 4. Detailed Findings

### 4.1 Trend Block

**200 SMA — 73,179.53 (long-term regime: repaired, slowly rising).** Price is **+9.47%** above it. The 200 SMA has climbed steadily from 69,683.99 (2026-09-05) to 73,179.53 (2026-11-04), and has been ticking up ~+20–30 points/day — the long-term average is still absorbing the H1 2026 crash. The **golden cross completed between 09-07 and 09-08** (values above) and remains intact; the 50 SMA sits **12.03% above** the 200 SMA. Interpretation: the macro downtrend that defined H1 2026 has structurally flipped positive — dips toward the low-$73Ks would be strategic support tests, not regime breaks.

**50 SMA — 81,986.29 (medium-term: the cap).** Price is **−2.29% below** it. After the steep September climb (69,094.75 → 81,702.07 by 10-21), the 50 SMA has **plateaued around $81.8K–$82.0K** for two weeks (81,782.29 on 10-22 → 81,986.29 on 11-04). It now coincides with the underside of October's trading shelf (daily closes of 81,311.89–84,011.97 through mid-October), making **~$82.0K a dense, multi-factor resistance zone**. Today's +3.58% thrust leaves ~1,875 points to that cap — the single most important near-term test.

**10 EMA — 78,826.26 (short-term trigger: freshly reclaimed).** On 11-03 the close (77,345.05) sat below the 10 EMA (78,540.81); today's close (80,110.81) is **+1.63% above** it. The 10 EMA itself is curling upward (78,540.81 → 78,826.26). This is the first short-term trend-flip since mid-October, but the 10 EMA is noise-prone — it needs the 50 SMA test to confirm.

### 4.2 Momentum Block

**MACD — −1,116.40 (bearish regime, but improving).** The line plunged from +2,014.20 (10-04) to −1,314.42 (11-03), the deepest negative reading of the 60-day window — confirming October's downtrend. It turned up today (−1,116.40). Against the signal line (**−937.13**, verified snapshot), MACD needs a **+179.27-point** improvement to trigger a bullish crossover; at the current one-day pace (+198.02), a crossover is arithmetically within reach within 1–2 sessions **if** the thrust continues. Until then, the momentum regime is formally bearish.

**MACD Histogram — −179.27 (the earliest positive signal).** The histogram has contracted three consecutive sessions: **−479.68 (11-02) → −422.11 (11-03) → −179.27 (11-04)**. Momentum is decelerating to the downside even though the line is below zero — the classic precondition for a trend repair. Treat a zero-cross of the histogram as confirmation, not a standalone entry.

**RSI — 49.68 (recovered from near-oversold; mid-range, room in both directions).** RSI bottomed at **34.33 on 2026-10-30** — near, but not at, the 30 threshold, consistent with a grinding (not capitulating) decline — and has rebounded to 49.68 in two sessions (38.30 on 11-03 → 49.68 on 11-04). No overbought/oversold extreme and no divergence extremes in the window. The mid-50s October readings (56.68 on 10-21) preceded failure, so RSI alone is not bullish here — but there is ample headroom before any overbought constraint.

### 4.3 Volatility & Mean-Reversion Block

**Bollinger Upper Band — 84,343.92 (ceiling; +5.28% above close).** The verified snapshot gives the full band set: middle **80,188.85**, upper **84,343.92**, lower **76,033.77**. Today's action was textbook mean-reversion: the low (**75,709.91**) **traded below the lower band** and the close returned to the middle band. With price at the middle band and RSI below 50, the market is neither stretched nor exhausted — upside to the upper band (+5.28%) is unobstructed by band-related overbought conditions. Note the upper band has been compressing downward (86,501.82 on 10-16 → 84,343.92 on 11-04) — the bands are narrowing after the October slide, and the upper band now sits almost exactly at the **Oct 21 swing high zone ($84,011.97 close / $84,840.05 high)**, forming a confluence resistance at **~$84.3K–$84.8K**.

**ATR — 2,160.17 (elevated but cooling; size positions accordingly).** ATR is **2.70% of price**, down ~14% from the 60-day peak of 2,510.48 (2026-09-23) but well above quiet-market levels. Today's 5,036-point range (2.33× ATR) shows volatility expansion on the reversal — expect continued wide daily ranges. Practical implications:
- A **1.5× ATR stop ≈ 3,240 points** (~$76,870 from an ~$80,110 entry); a structural stop sits below the reversal low at **$75,709.91**.
- A 1× ATR daily move from the close spans roughly **$77,950–$82,270** — trades should not expect fills tighter than that.
- Position sizing should be scaled to ATR, not to fixed dollar stops, given 2%+ daily swings are routine.

### 4.4 Volume Observation

Reversal-day volume was ~**39.95B**, roughly **+78%** above the prior day (~22.41B) and the highest since the late-October selloff days (40.89B on 10-29, 45.89B on 10-30). Heavy volume on an up-thrust from the lower band is constructive — but one session is confirmation of *intent*, not yet of *trend*.

---

## 5. Key Levels (all from verified data)

**Resistance (ascending):**
1. **$81,986** — 50 SMA + underside of October's trading shelf (closes 81,311.89–84,011.97). Primary decision level.
2. **$83,500–$84,800** — Bollinger upper band (84,343.92) overlapping the Oct 21 swing high (84,840.05) and Oct 2 high zone.
3. **$87,100–$87,400** — September 21 recovery high (87,363.76) and October 2 high (87,146.35). Major supply.

**Support (descending):**
1. **$75,700–$76,270** — Nov 4 reversal low (75,709.91), Nov 3 low (76,270.00), lower Bollinger band (76,033.77). Invalidation zone for the reversal thesis.
2. **$73,180** — 200 SMA (73,179.53). Strategic line in the sand; a break would reopen the macro downtrend question.
3. **$62,400–$65,000** — February/March 2026 low zone (Feb 24 low 62,553.19; Feb 5 low 62,353.54).
4. **$57,700–$58,600** — 2026 yearly floor (Jul 1 low 57,747.77; Jun 30 close 58,558.86).

---

## 6. Actionable Scenarios

- **Bull continuation (requires confirmation):** Hold above the 10 EMA (~78,826) and push through the **50 SMA at ~81,986** on sustained volume, with MACD crossing its signal (needs +179.27) and ideally zero. First target: the **84,344 upper-band / 84,840 swing-high confluence**; extension toward 87,146–87,364. Until the 50 SMA is reclaimed, treat rallies as counter-trend within October's lower-high structure.
- **Bear resumption:** A daily close back below **76,034 (lower band)** — i.e., failure to hold the reversal low — would negate the mean-reversion signal and open a retest of the **200 SMA at 73,180**, with the 50 SMA's plateau at ~82K then acting as confirmed supply.
- **Neutral chop:** Closes oscillating between ~78,800 (10 EMA) and ~82,000 (50 SMA) would simply extend the repair phase; ATR-based range trading, not trend-following, is the appropriate playbook there.
- **Risk management:** With ATR at 2,160 (2.70% of price), use ATR-multiple stops (1.5–2.0×), size positions so a 2× ATR adverse move is an acceptable loss, and expect 4,000–5,000-point daily ranges to persist near-term.

1. **2026-11-04 close:** `get_stock_data` returned **80,118.23**, while the verified snapshot returns **80,110.81** (volume: 39,949,910,016 vs 39,951,306,752). Difference is ~0.009%; **the verified snapshot values are used throughout this report** per the source-of-truth rule.

---

## ⚠️ Data Availability Notice (read first)

Three data sources could not be retrieved during this analysis cycle and I am explicitly flagging them rather than estimating values:

1. **Asset-specific news for BTC-USD** — the news vendor failed twice (`YFDataException`). No BTC-specific headlines could be sourced this week.
2. **FRED macro series** (CPI, fed funds rate, 10Y Treasury, unemployment) — unavailable (`FRED_API_KEY` not configured). All macro commentary below is therefore grounded in **news headlines and live prediction-market pricing**, not official government data.
3. **Prediction markets for "recession 2026" and "crypto regulation"** — Polymarket returned HTTP 429 (rate-limited) on three attempts. Only the Fed-cuts and Bitcoin market queries succeeded (captured before throttling began).

Everything below is based on successfully retrieved data only.

---

## 1. Executive Summary

The macro backdrop this week is **risk-on and disinflationary, but with the Fed fully priced on hold** — a combination that historically supports risk assets without providing the liquidity-cut catalyst crypto bulls want. The single most important finding for BTC-USD: **prediction markets have essentially fully priced zero Fed rate cuts for 2026 (98% "Yes" on "no cuts")**, and simultaneously **faded the odds of a year-end Bitcoin rally to $100K to just 14%, down 4pp in one week**. Meanwhile, broad-market signals (VIX below 18, Treasury yields dipping post-midterms, oil down ~8%) point to a calm, low-volatility environment.

**Net read: a supportive macro tape with no rate-cut tailwind — favoring range-bound, low-volatility trading in BTC-USD over momentum plays, with a mildly negative short-term drift implied by the one-week markdown of upside odds.**

---

## 2. Macro Environment — Rates, Inflation, Liquidity

**What we can and cannot say.** Direct FRED prints (CPI, fed funds, 10Y) could not be retrieved (API key missing). The macro picture below is triangulated from market prices and financial headlines.

- **Fed path: hard freeze through 2026.** The deepest-liquidity Polymarket market — *"Will no Fed rate cuts happen in 2026?" — is at 98% Yes* on **$9.4M volume**, and *rose* +0.9pp over the week. Every cut-count market (6, 9, 10, 11, 12+) is priced at 0%. This is as close to a certainty as markets offer: **no monetary easing catalyst is coming in the remaining ~8 weeks of 2026.** For BTC-USD — an asset whose bull cycles have historically been fueled by easing liquidity — this removes the classic year-end rally fuel.
- **Long-end yields drifting lower.** The headline *"Housing stocks rally following midterm elections, Treasury yields dip lower"* indicates the midterm outcome was received as rate-friendly, pulling yields down. Softer long rates are a partial offset to the no-cuts freeze — they ease financial conditions without the Fed moving.
- **Disinflationary energy impulse.** *"Oil sinks nearly 8%"* in the past week is a meaningful disinflationary shock. It pressures headline inflation lower and, over time, weakens the case for a restrictive Fed — a latent dovish optionality that isn't priced in the 2026 cut markets (which resolve Jan 1, 2027 and only cover cuts executed in calendar 2026).
- **Volatility compressed.** *"VIX drops below 18"* with blue chips surging (>2.8% per the headline) signals broad risk appetite and low cross-asset stress. In this regime, crypto historically chops rather than trends violently.
- **The AI trade still dominates equity narrative flow** (IBM quantum encryption on Heron R2, Adobe's AI integrations, Confluent, Accenture coverage). Capital continues concentrating in AI-linked tech — a competing magnet for the speculative dollar that in prior cycles has sometimes drained crypto-adjacent flows.

---

## 3. BTC-USD Positioning — What Prediction Markets Imply

This is the richest dataset available this week. Reading the market structure carefully:
